newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 27.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Financial services group Capital Alliance clinched a 2.8 billion rand deal for the 34.9 percent controlling stake in Anglo American's mining house JCI, beating New Africa Investments' bid.

- Anglo American boosted headline earnings 22 percent to 2.4 billion rand for the six months to September after strong performances from its diamond and coal investments and a turnaround in its gold interests.

- Union federation Cosatu is to call on the African National Congress to enter negotiations on an "alliance accord" intended to resurrect a working alliance and commit government to an agreed programme of action.
- The gold price continued to slide on Tuesday to test a two-year low, prompting a sell-off on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange that trimmed three percent or 48 points off the all gold index.

- Safety and security minister Sydney Mufamadi has apppinted well-known human rights campaigner and an outspoken critic of South Africa's gun laws, Sheena Duncan, to head a committee of inquiry into the running of a central firearms registry.
- The African Mining Group consortium, led by Mzi Khumalo's Capital Alliance Holdings, won the bidding to buy 34.9 percent of JCI from Anglo American from 54.50 rand a share.

- Cosatu's executive comittee has proposed sweeping economic measures, including freezing by government of management salaries in the private sector, the restructuring of the Reserve Bank and the capping of interest rates, as part of a package to resurrect the RDP (reconstruction and development programme).
- The rand stayed below the pyschologically important 4.60 level on the dollar on Tuesday, firming more than two cents to reach 4.5850.
- Foschini's profit record is under threat after the blue-chip retailer reported a worse-than-expected drop in interim profit on Tuesday.

- Strong performances by Anglo American's coal and diamond interests lifted its headline earnings 22 percent in the six months to September 30 to 2.4 billion rand, despite a weak performance by the industrial sector.

- Poor weather, dense vegetation and inhospitable terrain have been hampering the search for fugitive Mark Dewes who is being sought in connection with the frenzied shooting of two men and the wounding of two others in a remote forestry station.

- A Pretoria couple on honeymoon in the Comores hit the jackpot on Tuesday when they sold, for 400,000 rand, a video recording of the Ethiopian plane which crashed just 300 metres from where they sat on Saturday.
